approach: Add `check_job_size(reading)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs as a new `step!` in `refusing_check`, directly after `check_prior_result_and_scope`. For a change reading with no question, it counts deliverables other than CHANGELOG.md and the distinct surfaces they sit in: `docs`, `.github`, `xtask`, `crates/<crate>`, `root` for a file at the repo root such as athena.toml, or the top-level directory otherwise. It refuses above 8 deliverables or above 4 surfaces. The error says to split the job by surface and dependency: keep one dependency-ordered group, and name the rest in `out_of_scope` for a separate request. The doc comment names the root cause and jobs 20261025-183644-t67q and 20261017-205554-zaj2, and declares the refusal intended with the share "expected 6% of newly refused readings". Tests go in reading.rs (shapes of both failed jobs, bound and skip cases, one-step-line, doc and changelog pins), and refusing and accepting cases go in refusal_corpus.rs. CHANGELOG.md gets one entry. No prompt, config or workflow file changes; the refusal text carries the repair, and `Athena::read_for` re-reads with it. The producer no-change guard is out of scope.

decisions.choice: Measure the property on `Reading.deliverables` directly (count and distinct surfaces), in the reading gate, as a `step!` in `refusing_check`.
decisions.reason: The gate is the one place that runs before dispatch and holds the full deliverable list. Both failed jobs had 9 or more non-changelog deliverables over 5 or more surfaces. A step there is covered by the corpus mechanism `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` and by the replay, and the refusal text goes back to the reader through `read_for`.

rejected.option: A guard on the producer's no-change outcome (run/producer.rs, send_back.rs).
rejected.why: It acts after a full producer run has been spent. The brief puts it out of scope, and `run/producer.rs` already reports a no-change outcome.

rejected.option: Count words or criteria in the request text.
rejected.why: A proxy. The deliverable list is the real measure of surfaces, and the request text can be short for a large job.

rejected.option: Split the request automatically into several jobs.
rejected.why: Out of scope. It needs a job-creation and ordering design, while refusing with a repair uses the existing retry path.

decisions.choice: Bounds are 8 deliverables (CHANGELOG.md excluded) and 4 surfaces, as named constants `MAX_JOB_DELIVERABLES` and `MAX_JOB_SURFACES`. Tests at the bound pass and one past it fail.
decisions.reason: The failed jobs had 9 and 11 non-changelog deliverables and 5 or more surfaces. The largest deliverable list in the existing corpus and unit tests is 3 paths. The numbers are a design choice and are declared as such.

rejected.why: Few files across docs, config, CI, xtask and a crate is the separable shape in 20261017-205554-zaj2's prevention text. The surface bound catches it.
Twelve files in one crate also overran a producer run, so the count is needed on its own.

decisions.reason: A reading that must be split makes the later repairs (governance, scope limit, boundary) moot, so the reader should be told to split first. The retry/prior check stays first because it needs the earlier attempt. No existing adjacency test pins a neighbour of this position: the adjacency tests pin survey to history_fixture, outcome_state to environment_reach, governance to outcome_state and environment_reach to defined_terms (reading.rs:4785, 5268, 7291, 7990).

rejected.why: The reader would first be sent to repair governance and scope-limit text in a reading that is then refused for size, costing a read round.

decisions.choice: Skip readings with `capability != Some("change")` or with a question, as `check_scope_limit` does (checks.rs:706).
decisions.reason: Study readings produce no change to measure, and a reading with a question has no accepted scope yet.

rejected.why: A study reading with many files read would be refused wrongly.

decisions.choice: Surface is computed by a private helper `job_surface(path)` that applies `normalized_path` (checks.rs:775) first, so `./docs/x.md` and `docs/x.md` match; a directory deliverable `crates/athena-cli/tests/` maps to `crates/athena-cli`. Tests under a crate stay in that crate's surface.
decisions.reason: Reuses the existing path normalizer. Counting a crate's tests apart would split one coherent crate change into two surfaces.

rejected.why: Almost every code change has a crate and its tests, so most would reach 3 surfaces with a docs file. It would raise the false-refusal rate.

risks.risk: An existing test reading exceeds 8 deliverables or 4 surfaces and is now refused as too large.
risks.mitigation: I searched for readings with long deliverable lists in reading.rs, refusal_corpus.rs, steward.rs, run/tests.rs and drain.rs (single-line and multi-line patterns) and found none: the largest list read is 3 paths (corpus `landing-rule-on-job-commits-only-job-1rve`). Criterion 6 runs the whole suite; a failure there names the reading. The fix is to shrink that fixture, never to raise the bound.

risks.risk: The bounds (8 and 4) refuse a legitimate focused job, for example a rename across a crate with 9 files.
risks.mitigation: The refusal is a repair request, not a dead end: the error says to keep one dependency-ordered group and name the rest in `out_of_scope`. The share is declared (6%, an estimate, not measured) and the verification replay measures it. The bounds are two named constants, so a later change is one line and the at-the-bound tests move with it.

risks.risk: The reader cannot repair a reading whose request really spans many surfaces, so it is refused repeatedly.
risks.mitigation: A refused reading goes back to the reader once with the refusal text (`Athena::read_for`), and the repair is to narrow the scope with `out_of_scope` items, which existing checks accept. Automatic splitting stays out of scope.

risks.risk: A retry whose carried-over earlier files (`check_prior_result_and_scope`) must all be covered exceeds the bound.
risks.mitigation: That check runs first, so its message comes first; the size check then refuses a still-too-large retry. This is intended, since the job is too large for one run. The retried jobs named in the brief left no candidate, so none applies today.

risks.risk: Directory deliverables, `./` prefixes, root files and crate-relative paths (`src/reading.rs`) are miscounted as surfaces.
risks.mitigation: `job_surface` uses `normalized_path` first and handles each form explicitly; `job_size_bound_is_general` has a case for each: `./docs/a.md` equals `docs/a.md`, `crates/athena-cli/tests/` is crates/athena-cli, a root file is `root`, `src/reading.rs` is `src`, and CHANGELOG.md is not counted.
